learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the magic element 'Carbon' that forms the basis of all life through its unique ability to bond with itself infinitely!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Unlike metals that give away electrons, Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell (Tetravalency) and needs 4 more. So, it *shares* electrons with other atoms to form strong Covalent bonds.
Carbon is unique because of 'Catenation'—its ability to form long chains, branches, and rings by bonding with other carbon atoms. This is why there are millions of carbon compounds!
Compounds of carbon and hydrogen. Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes) have only single bonds. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have double (Alkenes) or triple bonds (Alkynes) between carbon atoms.
A series of compounds with the same functional group (like Alcohol -OH, or Carboxylic acid -COOH) where each successive member differs by a -CH₂ unit. They have similar chemical properties.

Soap molecules have two ends: a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-hating, dirt-loving) tail. They trap dirt inside a spherical structure called a 'Micelle', which washes away with water.

fun_activity.title: ✏️ The Graphite Circuit
fun_activity.instructions: Graphite is an allotrope of carbon. Take a pencil (which has a graphite core) and sharpen both ends. If you connect it to a small battery and an LED bulb using wires, the bulb will glow! Graphite conducts electricity!

exam_tips: 📌 Be able to draw the electron dot structures for simple molecules like CH₄, CO₂, and O₂.
📌 Remember that Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulas.
📌 Understand why soaps don't work well in hard water (they form an insoluble scum), but detergents do.
quick_recap: ⭐ Diamond and Graphite are both made of pure carbon (allotropes), but their different structures make one hard and the other soft.
⭐ Ethanol (alcohol) and Ethanoic acid (vinegar) react to form sweet-smelling Esters.
⭐ Addition reactions occur only in unsaturated hydrocarbons (like turning vegetable oil into ghee).
